key_insight: This survey connects video understanding, video generation, and world modeling through one idea: video is a partial, imperfect view of a world that changes over time. This perspective helps explain how these research directions relate to one another.
problem_solved: Video foundation models and video world models are often studied separately despite overlapping goals. The survey offers a shared conceptual framework for examining their relationship.
method: Adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for reviewing video foundation models and video world models.
Treats video as a partial, lossy, temporally ordered observation of an underlying evolving world.
Contrasts understanding and generating visual sequences with modeling the dynamics behind those sequences.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this framing clarifies the distinction between modeling visible video content and modeling underlying world dynamics. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific conclusions and empirical findings cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Projection diagram: an evolving world produces a limited sequence of observed video frames.
Comparison panel: video understanding, video generation, and world dynamics modeling.
Timeline: visible frames above an underlying world-state trajectory, with hidden information highlighted.
Concept map: world modeling as the bridge between video foundation models and video world models.
paper_title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
paper_authors: Shengqiong Wu, Meng Luo, Bobo Li, Ziwei Liu, Shuicheng Yan
